title: Dedicated drain: add progress metrics + dashboard hooks
author: Sergio Costa
release_notes: Adds Dedicated drain progress metrics (percent/ETA/states) and emits annotations for dashboards during drain workflows. No customer-facing API changes.
description: Context: As part of the regional failover automation upgrade, we added a Dedicated pool drain workflow (PR #19822) but on-call has had limited visibility into whether a drain is making forward progress vs stuck (and how close we are to a safe cutover). This PR adds drain progress metrics emitted by the drain coordinator and wires those metrics into the existing failover signal dashboards so the game day runbook can validate drain progress in real time. What’s included: 1) New metrics for Dedicated drain lifecycle and progress, emitted from the dedicated-drain coordinator and keyed by pool_id (bounded) + region + customer_tier. 2) A periodic progress sampler that computes remaining nodes/replicas, in-flight request counts, and an ETA based on recent completion rate; sampler is explicitly best-effort and will not block drain execution. 3) An annotation event emitted when a drain starts/stops/aborts (to reduce manual timeline stitching). 4) Dashboard hooks: update the failover dashboards spec wiring (Grafana json in observability-pack is handled in PR #907; this PR provides the metric contract and internal dashboard wiring behind the same feature flag). Metric definitions: - dedicated_drain_state{region,pool_id,tier,state}: gauge (0/1) for states: requested|running|paused|completed|aborted|failed. - dedicated_drain_progress_percent{region,pool_id,tier}: gauge 0..100 (reported as float; rounded in dashboard). - dedicated_drain_remaining_nodes{region,pool_id,tier}: gauge. - dedicated_drain_inflight_requests{region,pool_id,tier}: gauge from gateway/routing counters (best-effort snapshot). - dedicated_drain_eta_seconds{region,pool_id,tier}: gauge; -1 when unknown (e.g., insufficient samples). - dedicated_drain_transition_total{region,tier,reason}: counter (pool_id intentionally excluded to keep cardinality bounded; pool_id is available via logs/audit events). Cardinality + safety: pool_id is bounded by Dedicated pools and is already an existing bounded identifier in internal metrics; we enforce a max distinct pool_id per region in the emitter (drops + logs once exceeded). We intentionally do not label by tenant_id/customer_id. For event-style visibility and audits, the drain workflow already emits audit events; this PR adds a short annotation emitter that references the audit event id. Testing: unit tests cover ETA calculation behavior (including noisy/stalled progress) and state transitions; integration test uses the staging drain simulator to ensure gauges get updated and cleared on completion/abort. Rollout: guarded by feature flag dedicated_drain_progress_metrics (default off). We’ll enable in staging during rehearsal; production enablement will be scoped to game day allowlist tenants/pools per ENG-2420 and the runbook checklist. Follow-ups: - Add an alert on “drain running with no progress > N minutes” once we have staging data (tracked in ENG-2426). - Add better correlation to incident timeline tooling (planned in PR #19844).

runbooks (internal refs): update metric queries used by Hosted/Dedicated failover checklist
notable_snippets: New metric names (summary): dedicated_drain_progress_percent, dedicated_drain_remaining_nodes, dedicated_drain_eta_seconds, dedicated_drain_state{state=...}, dedicated_drain_transition_total{reason=...}
ETA behavior: uses last 5 progress samples (min 90s window); returns -1 when rate is ~0 or insufficient samples; clamps to [0, 24h] to avoid crazy dashboards during partial telemetry loss.
review_conversation: Allison Grant: Please confirm we’re not adding tenant/customer labels here; pool_id seems OK but I’m worried about high-cardinality if we include per-replica identifiers. Also: can eta_seconds be -1 vs NaN so alerts can treat it explicitly?

Sergio Costa (author): Confirmed: no tenant/customer id, no replica ids. Labels are region,pool_id,tier (+ state for the state gauge). eta_seconds returns -1 when unknown; dashboards will map -1 to “unknown”. Added a unit test to cover this path.
Vanessa Ortiz: How do we prevent this from becoming a hot loop when drain is running for large pools? Also ensure we don’t make drain completion dependent on metric emission.

Sergio Costa (author): Sampler runs every 15s with jitter; uses cached coordinator state and a single aggregated read for inflight. Errors are swallowed and logged; drain state machine does not await metric emission. Added a benchmark and a note in code comments.

Miles Thornton: For the transition counter, can we standardize reason values with the rollback ADR language (abort, rollback, capacity_gate, operator_cancel) so dashboards are consistent with failover controller metrics?

Sergio Costa (author): Good call—updated reason enum to align with controller audit reasons + documented allowed values; also added a mapping for legacy abort codes to keep compatibility with existing logs.
Rafael Mendes: Please add a quick query example in the PR description or code comment for on-call: how to tell “stuck drain” vs “paused drain” and where to look.
Sergio Costa (author): Added query examples in a comment near metric definitions and updated the internal runbook reference section with two PromQL snippets.
